correctness.rationale: Exact ninth-degree polynomial factorization gives all nine roots; exact differentiation yields multipliers 9/2, zero on four roots, and 27±18√2 on four others, all strictly away from the unit circle. Four roots attract and five repel locally. The two-step nonminimum orbit and 5/32 mean loss are exact identities. Simplicity of all roots, polynomial degree nine and continuous multipliers give nine real persistent roots with identical stability split throughout an open parameter neighborhood via the implicit-function theorem. The standalone SymPy checker executed and reproduced these identities. No global attractor claim is made.

Neither entails an exact off-minimum superattracting two-phase orbit for a nonconvex quartic objective.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Local attraction at minimizers cannot rule out coexisting attracting states elsewhere. Quadratic schedules have no nonminimum finite orbit under the proven linear-contraction assumptions. The claimed nonminimum stable orbit is a different nonlinear global phenomenon.

value.rationale: The rates are intrinsically motivated landmarks: 2 is the exactly chaotic Chebyshev endpoint for a constant step; 1/2 is the zero-local-multiplier minimizer step. Their alternating composition has two robust nonoptimal superattracting two-phase orbits with positive average loss 5/32 simultaneous with two superattracting actual minima. The complete nine-epoch-fixed census plus open two-parameter persistence establishes natural multistability relevant to nonconvex cyclic optimization; it is not merely a finite numerical orbit, arbitrary unmotivated parameter slice, or a local stability tautology. No claim is made to general optimization guarantees.
